subject: Social Media
title: Brigading and Coordinated Attacks
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Brigading and Coordinated Attacks.

hook.text: A Discord server with 10,000 members picks a target. Within minutes, they flood every post, review, and inbox.

buildup.text: Brigading is coordinated harassment from organized groups. GamerGate and 4chan raids popularized the tactic.

discovery.text: Platforms can't detect brigading easily because each individual action looks normal. Coordination is hidden.

twist.text: Groups organize on one platform, attack on another, and celebrate on a third. No single company sees it.

climax.text: Targets describe it as warfare: hundreds of hostile notifications per minute. The phone becomes a weapon.

punchline.text: One angry person is noise. A thousand is an army.

quiz.question: Why is brigading hard for platforms to detect?
options: Individual actions look normal in isolation
